rationale:
Evidence: all 480 development trials (iterations 0-10) ended off track after exactly one line-loss event, with max_error about 0.061 m against the 0.06 m limit. That limit is the floor for any body_width up to 0.18 m, so widening the body cannot help. Oval progress sits at 0.11-0.115 whatever the speed (0.7 to 1.8), gain, sensor spacing or line-loss rule. Speed is therefore not the main lever. Only forward sensor placement (y 0.06 to 0.08) and the 7-sensor array moved s-bend and slalom progress, and s-bend progress has never exceeded 0.1475. Iteration 9 never raced, so the 0.8 speed / kd 1.0 / 12 mm footprint bundle is unverified.

Changes (kept small, since the failure point is fixed and I have no telemetry on where the line is lost): (1) mass 0.6 to 0.4 kg, the minimum allowed, to reduce yaw inertia so the body turns faster after the single line loss. (2) wheel_track 0.14 to 0.16 m, to soften the turn rate per unit of wheel differential and reduce overshoot past the 0.06 m limit. (3) base_speed 0.7 to 0.9, a compromise between the 0.7 (oval 0.11) and 1.0 (best score 50.39) results. (4) kd 0.8 kept for damping, kp 2.0 kept for steering authority, ki 0.05 kept small. (5) Sensing kept as in iterations 4-10: 7 sensors at y = 0.08 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, footprint 0.016 m, linear antisymmetric weights. line_loss stays search_right, which gave the best score so far.

Expected result: score near the current 50, with a modest chance of max_error below 0.06 m and progress above 0.15 on the s-bend and slalom. Completion within 3 s is unlikely. If the oval progress stays at about 0.115, the failure is in the track geometry or start condition, and sensing and gain changes cannot fix it.
